subject: The Thalamus Conducts the Sleep Symphony: New Brain-Wide Evidence for Memory Consolidation
script: From Agewell Brief: The Thalamus Conducts the Sleep Symphony: New Brain-Wide Evidence for Memory Consolidation. A large EEG-fMRI study reveals how slow oscillations and spindles coordinate hippocampal–cortical communication during deep sleep, with the thalamus as the conductor. Sleep is not a passive shutdown. It is an active, orchestrated state where the brain replays and consolidates the day's experiences. Read the full source-linked dispatch and primary study caveats at AgewellBrief.com.
